definitions.explanation: Fruit that has been preserved by removing most of its water content through sun-drying or dehydration. Includes items such as raisins, dried persimmons, dried mangoes, and prunes.

examples.japanese: {干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの}をおやつに{食|た}べる。
examples.english: I eat dried fruit as a snack.

examples.japanese: {干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの}は{栄養|えいよう}が{凝縮|ぎょうしゅく}されている。
グラノーラには{干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの}やナッツが{入|はい}っていて、{朝食|ちょうしょく}にぴったりだ。
examples.english: Granola contains dried fruit and nuts, making it perfect for breakfast.

notes:
Composed of {干|ほ}し (dried, from the verb {干|ほ}す) and {果物|くだもの} (fruit). In modern Japanese, the loanword ドライフルーツ is very commonly used alongside the native term. {干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの} tends to evoke traditional Japanese dried fruits like {干|ほ}し{柿|がき} (dried persimmon), while ドライフルーツ often refers to imported or Western-style products.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの}を{作|つく}る: to make dried fruit
- {干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの}{入|い}り: containing dried fruit
- {無添加|むてんか}の{干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの}: additive-free dried fruit

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ドライフルーツ: dried fruit — the loanword equivalent; more common in commercial contexts
- {干|ほ}し{柿|がき}: dried persimmon — a traditional Japanese dried fruit
- {乾物|かんぶつ}: dried goods — a broader category including dried vegetables, seaweed, and mushrooms
